question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to $\sin(x + 4)\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}-\left(4 x + 16\right)\sin(x + 4)=\cos(x + 4)$ that satisfies $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})=\frac{3 \pi^{2}}{2}$. Assume that $-4<x<-4 + \pi$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first rearrange and separate, then integrate and apply the initial condition.

$$
y'=\frac{\cos(x + 4)}{\sin(x + 4)}+4 x + 16.
$$

Use $v=\sin(x + 4)$, so $\mathrm{d}v=\cos(x + 4)\mathrm{d}x$. On the given interval, sine is positive. Thus

$$
\int\mathrm{d}y=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{v}+\int \left(4 x + 16\right)\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
y=\ln(\sin(x + 4))+2 \left(x + 4\right)^{2}+C.
$$

At $x=-4 + \frac{\pi}{2}$, $\sin(x + 4)=1$ and hence

$$
\frac{3 \pi^{2}}{2}=\frac{\pi^{2}}{2}+C,\qquad C=\pi^{2}.
$$

Therefore $y=2 \left(x + 4\right)^{2} + \ln{\left(\sin{\left(x + 4 \right)} \right)} + \pi^{2}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-4(x + 4){y}^{2} & =4(x + 4) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4(x + 4){y}^{2}+4(x + 4) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4(x + 4)({y}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y & =4(x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y & =\int 4(x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1) & =2{(x + 4)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Exponentiating both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1)} & ={e}^{2{(x + 4)}^{2}+C} \\ {y}^{2}+1 & =C{e}^{2{(x + 4)}^{2}} \\ y & =\sqrt{C{e}^{2{(x + 4)}^{2}}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $y>0.$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-4)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-4) & =1 \\ \sqrt{C{e}^{2(0)^{2}}-1} & =1 \\ \sqrt{C-1} & =1 \\ C-1 & =1 \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=\sqrt{2{e}^{2{(x + 4)}^{2}}-1}.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-(x - 4)-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-(x - 4)}{e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-(x - 4)} \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{-(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int {e}^{-(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & =-{e}^{-(x - 4)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the natural logarithm to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-{e}^{-(x - 4)}+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-{e}^{-(x - 4)}+C).\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the condition $y(4)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(4) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(-{e}^{0}+C) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(C-1) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ C-1 & =\frac{1}{4} \\ C & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{-(x - 4)-y}$ that satisfies the condition $y(4)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}-{e}^{-(x - 4)}).
$$

We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{-y} & =6{(x - 4)}^{2}{e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{(x - 4)}^{2}{e}^{-y}-{e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(6{(x - 4)}^{2}-1){e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =(6{(x - 4)}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int (6{(x - 4)}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & =2{(x - 4)}^{3}-(x - 4)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the natural logarithm to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{(x - 4)}^{3}-(x - 4)+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{(x - 4)}^{3}-(x - 4)+C)\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(5)=0$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(5) & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot {1}^{3}-1+C) & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(1+C) & =0 \\ C & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{(x - 4)}^{3}-(x - 4)).

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3}$ that satisfies $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}(3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3}) \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3} \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =3\int {(x + 4)}^{2}\,\text{d}x-4\int {(x + 4)}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & ={(x + 4)}^{3}-{(x + 4)}^{4}+C \\ y & =\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{4}-{(x + 4)}^{3}-C}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-2) & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{{2}^{4}-{2}^{3}-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{8-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}$ is

$$
y=\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{4}-{(x + 4)}^{3}}\,.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4{y}^{2}}{{(x - 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}(\frac{4}{{(x - 4)}^{2}}+1) \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =(4{(x - 4)}^{-2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {y}^{-2}\,\text{d}y & =\int (4{(x - 4)}^{-2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ -{y}^{-1} & =-4{(x - 4)}^{-1}+(x - 4)+C \\ -\frac{1}{y} & =-\frac{4}{(x - 4)}+(x - 4)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $y$, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & =\frac{4}{(x - 4)}-(x - 4)-C \\ \frac{1}{y} & =\frac{4-{(x - 4)}^{2}-C(x - 4)}{(x - 4)} \\ y & =\frac{(x - 4)}{4-{(x - 4)}^{2}-C(x - 4)}\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(6)=-1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(6) & =-1 \\ \frac{2}{4-{2}^{2}-C(2)} & =-1 \\ \frac{2}{-2C} & =-1 \\ -\frac{1}{C} & =-1 \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=\frac{(x - 4)}{4-(x - 4)-{(x - 4)}^{2}}.
$$
